original_to_v2.before: The source-defined four-event L-lyxose 5-phosphate route joins RhaA isomerization, LyxK phosphorylation and successive 3- and 4-epimerization to D-xylulose 5-phosphate. Whole-route genetic support concerns adapted K-12 derivatives such as JA134 with plaR/yiaJ derepression; it does not establish complete flux in ordinary wild-type MG1655. SgbU remains a tentative 3-epimerase assignment after two negative enzyme assays. Native beta-L-lyxopyranose initiating chemistry is distinct from generic RhaT lyxopyranose transport; no anomerization is invented. The separate 1991 mutant-rhaB L-xylulose 1-phosphate route is excluded. AraD and SgbE are alternatives; frozen PathBank UlaF conflicts with native enzymes-not-used. Regulatory, metal, construct and source-access limits are preserved beside their edges.
original_to_v2.after: The source-defined four-event L-lyxose 5-phosphate route joins RhaA isomerization, LyxK phosphorylation and successive 3- and 4-epimerization to D-xylulose 5-phosphate. Whole-route genetic support concerns adapted K-12 derivatives such as JA134 with plaR/yiaJ derepression; it does not establish complete flux in ordinary wild-type MG1655. SgbU remains a tentative 3-epimerase assignment after two negative enzyme assays. Native beta-L-lyxopyranose initiating chemistry is distinct from generic RhaT lyxopyranose transport; no anomerization is invented. The separate 1991 mutant-rhaB L-xylulose 1-phosphate route is excluded. AraD and SgbE are alternatives; frozen PathBank UlaF conflicts with native enzymes-not-used. Regulatory, metal, construct and source-access limits are preserved beside their edges. PMID:10913096 additionally reports that pectinase-digested citrus or apple pectin increased the yiaJ/plaR-lacZ reporter 10-20-fold in ECL1, but not JA134. Structural-gene expression was unaffected even without the repressor, and the biological significance remained unresolved. Preparation: 0.14% pectin in sodium acetate, pH 4.0; overnight at 25 C with 400 U Aspergillus niger pectinase; tenfold dilution into medium. This undefined hydrolysate is retained as experimental context, without assigning an individual chemical or a PlaR-binding interaction.

after.subject: UniProtKB:P76268
after.description: Northern blots show increased plaR mRNA after deletion of KdgR, supporting a negative influence on plaR expression under these conditions. Regulation may be indirect; direct promoter binding is not established. Northern blots: BW25113 versus JW3546 (plaR deletion) or JW1816 (kdgR deletion); M9 + 0.5% casamino acids, 37 C, aerobic shaking, mid-exponential phase.

evidence.source_assertion: Northern blots show increased plaR mRNA after deletion of KdgR, supporting a negative influence on plaR expression under these conditions. Regulation may be indirect; direct promoter binding is not established.
Figure 5 compares BW25113 with plaR- and kdgR-defective derivatives in M9 plus 0.5% casamino acids, 37 C, aerobic shaking; RNA was sampled at mid-exponential phase for Northern blots.

Methods identify BW25113, JW3546 (plaR deletion) and JW1816 (kdgR deletion) for Northern blots. The K-12 protein and MG1655 gene accessions provide reference identities; the reported experiment used these BW25113 derivatives.
The issuing K-12 protein record links kdgR protein P76268 to NCBI Gene 946129; the protein identity is distinct from the measured gene-expression target.

The issuing MG1655 NCBI Gene record grounds kdgR/b1827 as the KdgR regulator subject's reference gene. The separately cited UniProt GeneID join identifies the protein subject; the expression target is plaR (Entrez:948084), and assay observations remain scoped to BW25113 derivatives.
The issuing K-12 protein record links plaR protein P37671 to NCBI Gene 948084; the protein identity is distinct from the measured gene-expression target.
The issuing MG1655 NCBI Gene record identifies plaR and its locus tag. This grounds the gene-expression endpoint while preserving the BW25113 assay-strain limitation.
